name: Hewitt Hall
use: College of Health and Human Services (administration, classrooms, labs)

renovations.what: U-shaped building renovated and 'filled in' (after three earlier renovations)
Major renovation in the early 1990s; 'New Hewitt Hall' reopened March 1994

facts.text: Built in 1893 as the Shops Building and renamed in 1942 for Charles E. Hewitt, the first electrical-engineering student and later first dean of engineering.
CHHS lists its address as Hewitt Hall, 4 Library Way.

verdict: The 1893 Shops building, rebuilt in the 1940s and again in 1994 as a long plain brick block for Health and Human Services.
notes: The old data's '$4.1M' 1994 cost and the TNH claim that CHHS 'outgrew' Hewitt were not verified. Search snippets say a 2026 UNH article mentions a home-care simulation space in Hewitt; not opened. No licensed modern photo; archives ref-01 (July 2016, color) shows a long three-story red-brick block with an arched entry. The historic images show the 1893 shops, which bear little resemblance to today's building.
judgeNotes: Archives photo shows a long three-storey brick front; licensed images are only distant 1901/1909 views.
